chapter: Gene Mayl, Teddy Buckner and the Dixie Flies
title: Forming Joe Darensbourg and His Dixie Flies
summary: Offered a restaurant job at the Lark, Joe led his own band for the first time in Los Angeles, partly to escape Happy Cunwith and the Four Hundred Club.

bands.name: Joe Darensbourg and His Dixie Flies

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Folk(?)? I don't know. Maybe it was Crescent(?)... Whatever it was. Maybe we can check that out.

I think we made three albums. After I stayed with Teddy for a while, I was supposed to put a band in the Lark. It was a restaurant actually over on Third Street, and the guy made me a terrific offer. That's when I organized my own band. This was about...
Is that why the record label was called Lark?

No, no, that didn't have nothin' to do with it. A lot of people ask that question. But the Swede and that guy... This guy Swede Jensen that started Lark Records, they just liked that title for some reason.
So in your band, the Dixie Flies it was called...
Who did you put in there.
Joe Darensbourg and His Dixie Flies.
Was that the first time you had a band under your own name?

Well, the first time in Los Angeles. I had had a band in Seattle. But the first time I really had a band here. In Seattle... I had gotten little jobs and picked up guys, but it wasn't a steady job. This was...
What made you decide to go into the bandleading business? You'd been a sideman practically all your life...

I really didn't want to do it. But Helen, my wife, tried to talk me into it, and these people, like I said, made me an offer that was good. And I just wanted to... I was having such a bad time, not really with Teddy but with a guy named Happy Cunwith(?) that owned the Four Hundred Club, I got so I didn't like him, and I wanted to get out of the band -- me and Harvey Brooks both.
